background.working_life: A 53-year-old employee working full-time in the construction sector, in metal forming, welding and related trades. The role is hands-on and classed as semi-routine, with no supervisory or management responsibilities. Weekly hours are long, at 49 or more, and the work is carried out at sites and premises rather than at home. Each journey to the workplace covers between 20 and 30 kilometres, made by car or van. Qualifications comprise five or more GCSEs or a vocational equivalent, with skills largely built through practical experience on the job.
background.home_and_household: Home is a semi-detached house in an urban part of the North West, owned with a mortgage still being repaid. Three adults live there and no dependent children, with any offspring now counted as non-dependent. Married and living as part of an opposite-sex couple, he is recorded as the husband of the household reference person. The occupancy rating for bedrooms stands at plus one, indicating one more bedroom than the household strictly requires, so the property offers a modest amount of spare space.
background.week_and_hobbies: Weekdays are shaped by early starts and long shifts, with a drive of around half an hour each way absorbing further time. Evenings tend to be quiet and spent at home, with television, radio, music or motoring interests filling the gap before an early night. Practical skills carry over into occasional repairs and improvements around the house and garden, and maintaining the car is a familiar task. Weekends allow more scope for rest, catching up with family, following sport results and local trips by road.
